Histopathological examination of skin biopsies showed slight acanthosis, focal parakeratosis, minimal and multifocal vacuolar degeneration of the basal layer, focal exocytosis of sparse lymphocytes, mild superficial perivascular and lichenoid lymphocytic infiltrates, and multifocal melanin‐laden macrophages with golden‐brown granules located both perivascularly and in other areas of the dermis (pigmentary incontinence) (Figure 2). in_text_mentions: The patient was a 13‐year‐old boy who presented with a several‐month history of progressively developing pruritic papules accompanied by desquamation and hypopigmentation of the trunk, thighs, and upper arms, with facial involvement (Figure 1). The patient was treated for pityriasis versicolor, but without improvement. Persistent symptoms without significant relief were observed. His medical history did not indicate any significant previous illnesses, and he had no known allergic reactions or comorbidities that could complicate his condition.

Mica-like scales were also observed in some of the lesions. Therefore, a punch skin biopsy was performed to confirm the diagnosis.
